diagnostic_evidence.quote: Minimizing the cut function alone is known to isolate single nodes when performing graph partitions

issues.failure_explanation: The display claims min NCut equals the minimum of x^TLx/x^TDx over the \pm1 indicator x. For x_i = \pm1, x^TLx = 4\,cut(A,B) and x^TDx = \sum_i d_i = vol(V), which is constant over partitions; hence the right-hand side equals (4/vol(V))\cdot\min cut(A,B), the plain minimum cut, not NCut = cut/assoc(A) + cut/assoc(B). Equality fails whenever the min-cut and min-NCut partitions differ (generic). The correct Shi-Malik identity uses the indicator y_i \in \{1, -vol(A)/vol(B)\} with constraint y^TD\mathbf{1} = 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the identity with the standard {1,-b}-valued indicator and the constraint x^TD\mathbf{1}=0, or replace the equality by the standard relaxation statement.
issues.overall_effect: Only the preliminary two-way motivation is false; the k-way definition \eqref{eq:NCut} and the relaxation \eqref{fairconst} used later are independent and unaffected.
issues.title: Two-way NCut equated with the wrong Rayleigh quotient
issues.why_classification: The false display is preliminary motivation with no downstream uses; the repair is a standard local restatement that preserves all substantive content.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma never defines H. The only H in the paper is the real-valued Stiefel embedding of \eqref{fairconst} (H^TH = I). The proof's key identities \sum_i f_i^{(s)}H_{i\ell} = |V_s \cap C_\ell| and \sum_i H_{i\ell} = |C_\ell| hold only when H \in \{0,1\}^{n\times k} is the cluster-membership matrix; for a general real H (e.g., eigenvector matrices with negative entries) both fail, so the stated equivalence is unsupported as written. The omitted hypothesis that H is the indicator matrix is essential.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the explicit hypothesis that H is the {0,1} cluster-membership matrix of the clustering (the standard setup of Kleindessner et al.), after which the proof is valid.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the linear fairness constraint F^TH = 0 used in \eqref{mainobj} is formally incomplete; Lemma \ref{lem:added-2} and the construction of F are independent of the defect.
issues.title: Fairness-constraint lemma omits the hypothesis that H is the 0/1 membership matrix
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard, forced hypothesis is a local clarification that validates the proof and leaves the paper's constraint formulation unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the eigenvalues of $Z^TGZ$ are all positive \cite{horn2013matrix}, and using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows:
Let $Z \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times (n-h+1)}$ denote an orthonormal basis for the null space of $F^T$.
we let $H =ZY$, where $Z$ is a projection to the null space of $F^T$ and $Z^TZ=I$.

issues.failure_explanation: Two invalid steps. (i) Z is n\times(n-h+1), non-square for h \ge 2, so Z^{-1} does not exist and 'Z^T = Z^{-1}' is meaningless. (ii) Even formally, passing from max_{Y^TY=I} Tr(Y^TZ^TGZY) to min_{Y^TY=I} Tr(Y^TZ^TG^{-1}ZY) requires (Z^TGZ)^{-1} = Z^TG^{-1}Z, i.e., G-invariance of ker F^T, which is generically false. Counterexample: n=3, F=(1,1,1)^T/\sqrt3, G = diag(1,2,3). With Z = [(1,-1,0)/\sqrt2, (1,1,-2)/\sqrt6], Z^TGZ = [[1.5,-0.289],[-0.289,2.5]] (top eigenvalue \approx 2.577) while Z^TG^{-1}Z \approx [[0.75,0.144],[0.144,0.472]] \neq (Z^TGZ)^{-1} \approx [[0.682,0.079],[0.079,0.409]] (bottom eigenvalue \approx 0.411, reciprocal \approx 2.434); the optimizers differ. Hence the maximizer of \eqref{SMW1} is not the minimizer of \eqref{SMW2}.

failure_location.quote: Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must delete the 'Z^T = Z^{-1}' step and retract the claimed equivalence of \eqref{SMW1} and \eqref{SMW2}, then either re-derive and justify the objective Fair-SMW actually computes (bottom eigenvectors of the fairness-restricted inverse) as a standalone method with its own guarantees, or replace the derivation with a correct constrained eigensolver (projection/deflation as in S-Fair-SC), abandoning the SMW-inversion reformulation.
issues.overall_effect: The reformulated problems \eqref{SMW3}, \eqref{SMW3b} and \eqref{reformulation} do not solve the advertised fair normalized-cut problem \eqref{mainobj}: Algorithm \ref{alg:smw-cluster} computes top eigenvectors of U = lim_{\mu\to\infty}(G^{-1}+\mu FF^T)^{-1}, i.e., solves min Tr(H^TG^{-1}H) over ker F^T, a materially different constrained spectral problem. The theoretical justification of Fair-SMW (and its RW/AFF variants) as a fair-clustering solver collapses; only the empirical results remain.
issues.title: Fair-SMW derivation uses Z^T = Z^{-1} for a tall Z and falsely claims (SMW2) is equivalent to (SMW1)
issues.why_classification: The equivalence is the keystone of the paper's main section and is false in general; no comparable version of the central claim survives from the source, and any repair requires essentially new proof architecture or a different algorithm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \min_{H} \left( \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}(H^T G^{-1} H) - \frac{\mu}{2} \text{Tr}(H^T F F^T H) \right) = \min_{H} \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}\left(H^T \left( G^{-1} - \mu F F^T \right) H \right)

issues.failure_explanation: The augmented Lagrangian is written with penalty -(\mu/2)||F^TH||_F^2 (the correct sign is +), so the 'penalty' rewards violating F^TH = 0. The derived stationarity equation (G^{-1} - \mu FF^T)H - F\Lambda = 0 inherits the wrong sign; the stated \Lambda=0 subproblem min_H (1/2)Tr(H^T(G^{-1} - \mu FF^T)H) is an unconstrained minimization of an indefinite quadratic, hence unbounded below with no minimizer; and the displayed block system is homogeneous, so it is solved by H = 0 and does not characterize the Stiefel-constrained minimizer. Equation \eqref{SMW3} then silently flips the sign to G^{-1} + \mu FF^T and reinstates H^TH = I, so it does not follow from the displayed derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the standard penalty sign + (\mu/2)||F^TH||_F^2, propagate it through the gradient and block system, and keep the constraint H^TH = I in the \Lambda=0 subproblem; then \eqref{SMW3} follows directly.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation presented as the justification for the Fair-SMW subproblem is internally contradictory; \eqref{SMW3}, which everything after uses, is asserted without valid support (though it is the standard quadratic-penalty/ALM subproblem).
issues.title: Augmented Lagrangian has the wrong penalty sign; (SMW3) flips the sign without justification
issues.why_classification: The endpoint \eqref{SMW3} is correct and is all that the rest of the paper uses; restoring the standard sign and constraint handling is a routine local edit with no loss of results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $G_{rw}$ has real eigenvalues and is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$
Therefore the eigenvalues of $B=\frac{1}{2}(D^{-1}W+WD^{-1})$ belong in $[-1,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs the symmetric part B = (1/2)(D^{-1}W + WD^{-1}) to have spectrum in [-1,1] and asserts |x^TD^{-1}Wx| \le x^Tx without proof. This is false: for the star K_{1,m}, B has eigenvalues \pm (m+1)/(2\sqrt m) (\approx 1.06 already for m=2; 2.6 for m=25). Consequently, for m \ge 14 the symmetric part C = B + 2I of G_rw has a negative eigenvalue (2 - 2.6 = -0.6 at m=25), so x^TG_rwx < 0 for some x: the theorem's conclusion 'x^TG_rwx > 0' is false for general graphs. (The companion conclusion that G_rw has real eigenvalues in [1,3] is correctly proved via similarity to A_sym + 2I.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the theorem to graph classes where the symmetric part of G_rw is positive definite (e.g., regular or bounded degree-imbalance graphs), or drop the generalized-positive-definiteness claim and prove directly the invertibility of F^TG_rwF needed by the algorithm.
issues.overall_effect: The RW variant loses its proof that G_rw meets the positive-definiteness hypothesis of Theorem \ref{thm:added-1} (applied to G_rw^{-1}), so the claimed guarantee that the SMW penalty framework applies to G_rw is unsupported; for degree-imbalanced graphs such as K_{1,25} the statement fails outright.
issues.title: Theorem claiming G_rw is generalized positive definite is false (star-graph counterexample)
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated, but a limited weakening or a contained replacement argument leaves a comparable statement for the RW variant; the real-spectrum part survives and no other labelled result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D^{-1}$ is an invertible diagonal matrix, it is of full rank, and multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space $ \mathcal{R}(F^T D^{-1}) = \mathcal{R}(F^T) $

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's first step \eqref{eq:identity} claims F^TD^{-1} = F^TD^{-1}F(F^TF)^{-1}F^T on the ground that right multiplication by the invertible diagonal D^{-1} 'does not change the row space'. Right multiplication by an invertible matrix preserves the column space, not the row space; the identity holds iff every column of D^{-1}F lies in range(F), which fails whenever two vertices in the same protected group have different degrees. E.g., for the path 1-2-3 with V_1 = {1,2}, V_2 = {3} and F = (1/2,1/2,-1)^T: F^TD^{-1} = (1/2,1/4,-1) but F^TD^{-1}F(F^TF)^{-1}F^T = (11/24,11/24,-11/12). With the identity gone, the reduction of P to I - F(F^T\mathcal{W}F)^{-1}F^T\mathcal{W} is unjustified, \mathcal{W}P need not be symmetric, and the similarity argument for real eigenvalues collapses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a new, correct proof that U_rw has real eigenvalues (e.g., via an appropriate similarity to a symmetric matrix without invoking \eqref{eq:identity}), or restrict to graph classes where the identity holds (group-wise constant degrees).
issues.overall_effect: The reality of the spectrum of U_rw - required for the RW variant's 'top k eigenvectors corresponding to largest eigenvalues' step to be well defined - is left unproven; the RW variant's theoretical standing is incomplete.
issues.title: Reality of the eigenvalues of U_rw rests on a false row-space identity
issues.why_classification: Only the proof fails - the conclusion is not contradicted by the source and may hold - but the false identity is the load-bearing step of the only proof given, so re-establishing the result needs a genuinely new, though contained, argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$

issues.failure_explanation: With M = G_sym^{-1}F, step 3 builds G_sym - G_sym^{-1}F(F^TG_sym^{-1}F)^{-1}F^TG_sym, which is not the matrix U = G - GF(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG derived in the text (the limit of (G^{-1}+\mu FF^T)^{-1}). The two differ already for G = diag(2,1), F = (1,1)^T: the text's U = (2/3)[[1,-1],[-1,1]] satisfies UF = 0, whereas the algorithm's matrix [[4/3,-1/3],[-4/3,1/3]] maps F to (1,-1)^T \neq 0. Hence, as written, the computed matrix does not annihilate range(F), and its top eigenvectors need not satisfy the fairness constraint F^TH = 0; the RW and AFF variants produced 'by substituting G_sym' inherit the same step.

failure_location.quote: \State Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace step 2 by M = G_sym F, the single change forced by the paper's own formula U = G - GP with P = F(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG, after which the algorithm matches the derivation.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Algorithm \ref{alg:smw-cluster} does not implement the method derived in the text, and its fairness-enforcement mechanism (UF = 0, so top eigenvectors lie in ker F^T) fails; the stated fairness guarantee of the procedure is not delivered.
issues.title: Fair-SMW algorithm sets M = G^{-1}F, computing a different matrix than the derived U
issues.why_classification: The correction is a forced one-line edit directly dictated by the paper's own definition of U, and it restores the construction and all its guarantees with no other loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the quadratic form of the unnormalized Laplacian, normalized by the degree matrix, is bounded by 2

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives y^TLy / y^TDy \le 2 via Lemma \ref{lem:diff-square}, i.e., sup \le 2, but the theorem asserts sup = 2 for every weighted undirected graph. Equality holds only for bipartite graphs; e.g., for the unit-weight triangle the supremum equals \lambda_max(L_sym) = 3/2 < 2. The display therefore contradicts both its own proof and the prose sentence directly above it ('is bounded by 2').
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace '=' by '\le' in the display (optionally noting that equality characterizes bipartite graphs).
issues.overall_effect: The stated equality is false for non-bipartite graphs; no downstream result is damaged because Theorems \ref{thm:added-2} and \ref{thm:added-4} use only the proven [0,2] bound.
issues.title: Theorem claims sup of the normalized Laplacian Rayleigh quotient equals 2; the proof only shows it is at most 2
issues.why_classification: The proof establishes exactly the inequality that all downstream uses rely on; the repair is a local statement fix with no loss of content.
